2. The plaintiff-petitioner filed the two suits, one against his sister Marium and the other against his another sister Sharifunnessa for cancellation of licence and recovery of possession after evicting them from the respective suit premises which are 2 small huts about the decimals each. His case was that his father Oliullah Munshi gifted 39 acres of land to him by a registered deed of Hiba-bil-ewaj on receipt of Holy Quaran on 19.3.30 when he was a minor. His sister-defendant were allowed to live in 2 portions of the said .39 acres of land by creating huts as licensees. The plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 56 of 1958 earlier against a third party for declaration of his title to a portion of the land covered by the said deed of Hiba-bil-ewaj and for eviction of the defendant of that suit in which his sister defendants were impeladed as proforma-defendants; along with others. The said suit was decreed on contest against the principal defendant and ex-parte against the rest including his sister, decreed on contest ex-parte against the rest including his sister-defendants to vacate the suit lands which they failed to do. 

 5. In second appeal the High Court Division held that the declaration of title in Title Suit Nos. 56 of 1958 operates as a res judicata and unless the decree obtained in that suit is set aside it is binding on the defendants. But the plaintiff has not been able to prove that the defendants were his licensees. His title was declared in respect of a different portion of 39 acres of land and not in respect of the entire homestead covered by the Hiba deed and hence the plaintiff is required to get his title established in a properly constituted suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession within 12 years from the date of defendants entering into the suit premises. The appeals were dismissed. 

 6. Mr. Sultan Ahmed, learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner, submits that the respondents are estopped from raising the issue of the petitioner's right, title and interest in the land covered by the Hiba deed because of the decree in Title Suit No. 56 of 1958 and the learned Judges of the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that the petitioner has to establish his title again in respect of that portion of .39 acre of land which is not covered by Title Suit No. 56 of 1958.
